data.heading: Where it started
data.description: A million-core farm running below capacity, because job runtimes and resource needs were hard to predict.

blocks.title: Business problem
blocks.body: At this scale, resource optimization was hard. Job durations varied widely, which made resource allocation inefficient and left slots underused, and business units ran at utilization levels from under 50% up to 75%.

blocks.title: Technical barriers
blocks.body: CPU, memory, and core requirements were estimated manually for each job, which often meant over-provisioning or under-provisioning resources.

blocks.title: Agivant's role
blocks.body: Data discovery, predictive modeling, anomaly detection, and integration into the client's scheduling and resource allocation systems

data.heading: What Agivant built
data.description: Agivant began with in-depth consultations with the client's experts to understand their environment. Analysis of job data, execution patterns, and infrastructure usage identified the key optimization opportunities and finalized the use cases. Exploratory analysis examined data patterns and anomalies in job behavior and resource use, feature engineering selected and refined the inputs, and machine learning models were built to predict job runtimes, memory needs, and CPU and core requirements. Value in days and weeks.

blocks.title: Job runtime prediction
blocks.body: Models estimate job runtimes from historical data and job characteristics, so the client allocates resources more efficiently and reduces idle time.

blocks.title: Resource requirement forecasting
blocks.body: Models predict memory, CPU, and core requirements for each job, for optimal allocation with minimal waste.

blocks.title: Anomaly detection
blocks.body: AI algorithms detect unusual patterns in job behavior, identifying potential failures early and preventing costly downtime.

blocks.title: Data collection and processing
blocks.body: Pipelines collect, clean, and transform job data from logs, metrics, and job parameters.

blocks.title: Feature engineering
blocks.body: Relevant features extracted from the data improve the accuracy and reliability of the models.

blocks.title: Scheduler integration
blocks.body: Agivant worked closely with the client's engineering teams to integrate the models into existing scheduling and resource allocation systems.

blocks.title: Real-time monitoring
blocks.body: A monitoring system tracks model performance and raises alerts on any anomalies.

blocks.title: Continuous improvement
blocks.body: A feedback loop refines the models based on real-world performance data.

blocks.title: Before
blocks.body: Manually estimated resources, unpredictable runtimes, underutilized slots, and resources over- or under-provisioned.

blocks.title: After
blocks.body: Predicted runtimes and resource needs feeding the scheduler, proactive anomaly detection, and models refined on live data.

data.heading: Proof in production
data.description: A job enters the queue and the models estimate its runtime and its memory, CPU, and core needs, so the scheduler allocates what the job requires. If the job's behavior turns unusual, anomaly detection flags it before it becomes a failure. The monitoring system tracks every model's performance, and real-world results feed back to refine the next round of predictions. Across business units, slot utilization now reaches as much as 90%.

blocks.heading: Measured results
blocks.description: Increased efficiency with an improved user experience, reduced operational overhead, and higher throughput with faster time to market.

blocks.title: Reusable asset
blocks.body: The custom prediction models stay integrated with the client's scheduler and keep improving through the feedback loop on live performance data. Every build amplifies the next.

blocks.title: Challenges overcome
blocks.body: Building a deep understanding of a unique environment at a scale of 1 million cores and 80 petabytes, and predicting runtimes and resource needs for jobs whose durations varied widely.
